transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm feeling okay, thank you for asking. I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing some light exercise, like gardening, about 1 week after surgery. Just be gentle with yourself and avoid heavy lifting or bending. Also, make sure to wear protective eyewear while gardening.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you for letting me know. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using your preservative-free eye drops four times a day to help with dryness. If you're running out, you can ask your GP for more.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks! I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal to be sensitive to bright light after cataract surgery, especially in the first few weeks. Wearing sunglasses can help with this. If it's severe or causing you a lot of discomfort, we may need to assess it further.
